title: GOV-0138: author prd.schema.json's missing $defs and sweep the unresolvable-$ref class across schemas/
objective: Resolve the 44 $ref in schemas/prd.schema.json by authoring the $defs block they point at, state in-file that doing so does not make them enforced in-gate, and add the unscoped guard whose absence let the defect sit.
business_value: The file read as a VALID schema and failed only at use, because meta-validation does not resolve $ref targets. The guard closes the class rather than the instance; the in-file note stops a later reader citing a resolvable $ref as evidence the schema layer enforces anything.
in_scope: schemas/prd.schema.json: author $defs {text, strings, nonEmptyStrings} with a $comment stating in-gate non-enforcement
tests/test_badf_schema_refs.py: unscoped sweep across schemas/ plus aim proof, resolver in stdlib
out_of_scope: Any change to check_schema -- the walker gains no $ref branch here; #265 owns that decision
Widening the sweep beyond schemas/ (templates/ is also governed; a later scope call)
#306 and #304 -- queued, explicitly not folded in
acceptance_criteria: Every $ref in schemas/prd.schema.json resolves; the 44-ref count is asserted, not assumed
No schema in schemas/ carries an unresolvable $ref -- the sweep is UNSCOPED and its reach is asserted so it cannot pass vacuously

The $defs block states that check_schema has no $ref branch and that minLength is unimplemented too, so the definitions are inert in-gate; a test fails if check_schema ever grows a $ref branch, because the note would then be wrong
Gate behaviour is unchanged, established by reading check_schema's implemented keyword set by AST rather than by comparing the function to itself

test_obligations.claim: no schema in schemas/ carries an unresolvable $ref, over a reach that is asserted
the $defs block declares its own in-gate non-enforcement, and the claim is falsified if check_schema grows a $ref branch
